story.logline: Every rule you live by began as a few written pages; it becomes law only when both houses agree on the very same words.

question: How does a bill become a law?

source.title: Test fixture written for this repo
quotes: A bill must pass both houses in the same form before it goes to the head of state.

explain.caption: A new law starts as a written bill.
Every rule you live by started as a few written pages.
Someone introduces a bill, and the lower house debates it.
If most members vote yes, it moves to the upper house.
Both houses must agree on exactly the same words.
Once signed, it applies to everyone.
Now weigh what this means for you.

tradeoffs: Two houses slow laws down, which also gives more time to spot mistakes.
leftOut: Committees, amendments and court challenges are not shown.
questionsToAsk: Which house is debating the bill I care about right now?
